answer.rationale: Two candidate causal stories compete. (1) The release 2h ago is the newest change and the latency climb began ~90m ago, which fits a post-deploy regression; memory_b6 says canary gating has caught bad builds here before, and memory_b1 says a rollback cleanly cleared a post-release spike. (2) The degradation is confined to the primary region, which superficially points at regional_failover (memory_b2). I am deliberately discounting (2) for now: a release normally lands in all regions, so single-region confinement is weak evidence for a code cause but is also consistent with a region-local resource problem — and critically, failing over the primary while settlement writes are at daily peak is the one action that directly threatens the primary objective of not losing customer writes. In-flight write cutover is not reversible; a rollback is. memory_b2's record says traffic 'shifted cleanly' but says nothing about the write load at the time, so I cannot assume that outcome transfers to a write-heavy peak. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked when headroom was provisioned *ahead* of a known surge, not as a 90-minute-in rescue, and it does nothing if the cause is a bad build. route_read_replicas (memory_b5) targets read pressure on the primary; our symptom is write-path p99, so it is likely off-target. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) protected against an external partner failing; there is no partner-outage signal here, and tripping a breaker on our own write path risks shedding exactly the customer writes we must not lose. I spend the single verification on memory_b1 rather than the tempting memory_b2, because b1 is the load-bearing premise under the action I intend to take: I need the original record to tell me whether that rollback was actually causally confirmed (or merely coincident with recovery), whether the failure mode was latency or just errors, and whether 'prior build was stable' means tested at comparable write volume. If b1 turns out to be a coincidence-flavored or error-only case, my confidence in rollback drops sharply and regional_failover with write-drain protection becomes the live option in the next window. Scale is a small guarded test, not a broad rollout: revert on a bounded slice of primary-region write traffic with a hard abort and write-loss monitoring, so I get a causal read within minutes without betting peak settlement on an unverified diagnosis. Downstream value risk is real and I am flagging it: every one of these six memories is a success story with the failures pruned out, so the inherited record systematically overstates how reliably each lever works and says nothing about the conditions under which it worked. If I act and log another clean success, I harden that bias for the next session. Whatever I write forward should record the peak-write context, the competing regional hypothesis I did not test, and the fact that the diagnosis remained uncertain at commit time.
